subject: maths
title: Primary 4 Adding and Subtracting Fractions
seo_title: P4 Adding and Subtracting Fractions Worksheets: Free Primary 4 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Adding and subtracting fractions with denominators not exceeding 12 (one denominator a multiple of the other)
meta_desc: Free P4 maths practice: add and subtract fractions with like and related denominators, simplest form and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Make the denominators the same, then add or subtract only the numerators.
body_html:
Like denominators: add or subtract the numerators

When the denominators are the same, the parts are the same size. Add or subtract the numerators. The denominator does not change.

Example

27 + 37 = ?

Add the numerators: 2 + 3 = 5. Keep the denominator 7.

Answer: 57

Example

89 − 39 = ?

Subtract the numerators: 8 − 3 = 5. Keep the denominator 9.

Answer: 59

Related denominators: make the denominators the same

Halves and eighths are different sizes, so you cannot add them as they are. 8 is a multiple of 2, so change 12 into eighths. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number.

Example

12 + 38 = ?

2 × 4 = 8, so 12 = 48. Then 48 + 38 = 78.

Answer: 78

Example

56 − 13 = ?

3 × 2 = 6, so 13 = 26. Then 56 − 26 = 36 = 12.

Answer: 12

Answers greater than 1

If the answer is an improper fraction, write it as a mixed number.

Give the answer in simplest form

Divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number until you cannot divide any more.

CalculationWorkingSimplest form
18 + 5868, then divide 6 and 8 by 234
14 + 512312 + 512 = 812, then divide 8 and 12 by 423
78 + 38108 = 1 281 14

Subtracting from a whole

Write 1 whole as a fraction with the same denominator, such as 1 = 88.

Word problems: draw a model

Draw a bar for the whole amount. Mark the part you know and put “?” on the part you need to find. Then decide whether to add or subtract.

Example

Siti had 56 m of ribbon. She used 13 m. How much ribbon was left?

56 − 26 = 36 = 12.

Answer: 12 m

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
27 + 37 = 514 (adding the denominators)Keep the denominator: 57
12 + 38 = 48 (not making a common denominator)Change 12 to 48 first: 48 + 38 = 78
18 + 58 = 68 (not simplifying)Divide by 2: 34
45 + 35 = 75 (leaving an improper fraction)Write it as a mixed number: 1 25

faq.q: What is taught in P4 fractions for adding and subtracting?
faq.a: In Primary 4, students add and subtract proper fractions with denominators up to 12, where one denominator is a multiple of the other. They give answers in simplest form and write answers greater than 1 as mixed numbers.

faq.q: How do I explain adding fractions with different denominators to my child?
faq.a: Make the parts the same size first. For 1/2 + 3/8, change 1/2 into 4/8, then add: 4/8 + 3/8 = 7/8.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when adding fractions?
faq.a: Adding the denominators, as in 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/14. The parts are still sevenths, so the answer is 5/7.

faq.q: Is adding and subtracting fractions in the MOE syllabus for Primary 4?
faq.a: Yes. It is part of Fractions in the Primary 4 Standard Mathematics syllabus (MOE 2021). In Primary 5, students go on to unlike denominators and mixed numbers.

Jug A has 34 ℓ of bandung. Jug B has 58 ℓ of bandung. How much bandung is there altogether?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: 8 is a multiple of 4, so use 8 as the common denominator. Multiply the numerator and denominator by 2: 34 = 68. Add the numerators: 68 + 58 = 118. 118 is more than 1: 118 = 1 38. The answer is 1 38 ℓ. There is more than 1 ℓ.

items.q:
Devi poured 14 ℓ of water from a bottle into a cup. There was 512 ℓ of water left in the bottle. How much water was in the bottle at first?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: At first = poured out + left. 12 is a multiple of 4, so use 12 as the common denominator. Multiply the numerator and denominator by 3: 14 = 312. Add the numerators: 312 + 512 = 812. Simplify: divide the numerator and denominator of 812 by 4 to get 23. The answer is 23 ℓ.

items.q:
Arjun read 29 of a storybook on Saturday and 13 of it on Sunday. What fraction of the book did he read on the two days?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: 9 is a multiple of 3, so use 9 as the common denominator. Multiply the numerator and denominator by 3: 13 = 39. Add the numerators: 29 + 39 = 59. The answer is 59.

items.q:
A fish tank was 1112 full of water. Mr Kumar let out some water to clean it. Then the tank was 13 full. What fraction of the tank did he let out?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: Water let out = before − after. 12 is a multiple of 3, so use 12 as the common denominator. Multiply the numerator and denominator by 4: 13 = 412. Subtract the numerators: 1112 − 412 = 712. The answer is 712.
